I have been a regular customer for some time and have always loved coming here, which makes this review particularly disappointing to write.

Unfortunately, one member of staff consistently makes the experience feel unwelcome. On one occasion, after my bag had ripped, I politely asked whether I could have one of the small paper bags to carry a purchase. I completely understand that businesses have rules and procedures, and I would never expect special treatment. However, there is a significant difference between enforcing a policy and making customers feel unwelcome. Sadly, every interaction I have had with this particular member of staff has felt cold, dismissive, and unnecessarily confrontational.

It’s such a shame because I genuinely love this establishment and have been a loyal local customer. The food and atmosphere are wonderful, but the repeated negative interactions have made me reluctant to visit as often as I once did.

The boxing ring and combat sports classes shortly be removed, yet there has been no communication about these changes that will significantly impact many members. These facilities are a major reason why people joined in the first place.

What’s even funnier is that membership prices increasing while key facilities are being taken away. Asking members to pay more for less is not a good look.

The lack of transparency and respect shown to loyal customers is extremely disappointing.

one_star_reviews.text: I chose this place for my 9 year old’s piercings because of the fantastic reviews, but our experience didn’t live up to others’ and I feel more upset about it the further I get. The main problem is that the piercings are wonky (pics attached) - one is much further from the face than the other, and my daughter will have this for the rest of her life. I know Nasila recommends drawing your own dots before, but to be honest we thought she would be better than us - we are new to piercing. She made marks with a huge pen, so the dots were splurges. She also was quite clumsy on my daughter’s second ear - the clamp kept falling off. I was surprised she wasn’t more adept and swift after the child knows the pain of the first one. Also, the head of her left piercing fell off after two weeks. Luckily we were able to find it, re-sterilise it, and screw it back on without a tool (this also involved having to poke the stem back through a little bit, which was very painful). A gem on the right piercing fell out after three weeks. I’m surprised by this because the earrings - and the whole thing - were ludicrously expensive. The price is about triple that of a reputable tattoo parlour (where I now wish we’d gone). The website makes it look like a spa but it’s a residential address and more like a bedroom. The spray that you have to buy afterwards has no ingredients list. Overall, I feel duped. Nasila is nice, and I am sad to have to leave a review like this, but there are too many aspects I feel are worth mentioning to other parents. The positive thing is that they haven’t become infected.

Order Reference: A1687362

I used CIBT Visas to assist with obtaining a Saudi Arabian one-year multi-entry visa. Unfortunately, my experience was disappointing and unnecessarily stressful.

To be fair, email responses were generally prompt. However, I found the overall service expensive, confusing, and lacking transparency.

One of the first issues was discovering that the 0844 number listed on the CIBT website is a premium-rate number. I was charged over £8.00 simply to hear an automated message stating the office was closed.

The document checking process also caused delays. CIBT rejected my Saudi MOFA invitation letter, claiming it lacked reference numbers required to book the Tasheer appointment. This later proved to be incorrect, as the appointment was booked without those numbers being needed.

The most concerning issue involved payment handling. During registration, I authorised a £0.00 payment through my banking app, after which more than £820.00 was withdrawn from my account before an invoice had even been issued. This included consular fees that were ultimately paid directly inside the Tasheer Centre during my appointment. When I queried this, I received contradictory explanations from different staff members. Although the money was eventually refunded, the process lacked clarity and transparency throughout.

Ironically, the actual visa appointment at the Tasheer Centre was straightforward and efficient. In contrast, CIBT added very little practical value beyond acting as an expensive middleman. Even basic questions asked to the representative outside the centre were met with “you need to email the office.”

I also paid extra for passport return via Royal Mail Special Delivery after being advised not to use the Tasheer Centre’s cheaper DHL next-day service. Despite this, my passport was not returned the next day and was delayed over the bank holiday weekend.

Overall, I found CIBT Visas to be overpriced, unnecessarily complicated, and poor value for money. I would strongly encourage anyone considering using them for a Saudi visa application to carefully review all charges, payment authorisations, and exactly what services are actually being provided.

My experience with Lifestyle Property Agents began when I paid a holding deposit for a rental property. What should have been a straightforward process quickly turned into weeks of back‑and‑forth emails. The agency initially refused to refund the deposit, alleging “fraudulent payslips” based only on an AI flag from their referencing provider. No evidence of fraud was ever produced, and the application was closed simply due to non‑response.

Despite repeated requests for clarification, they maintained this position until I pressed them on the Tenant Fees Act 2019. Only then did they change course and agree to refund — but even at that stage attempted to deduct £61 for referencing costs, which are prohibited under the Act.

This drawn‑out process highlights a concerning pattern: Lifestyle Property Agents rely on tenants not understanding the law to justify keeping deposits. Their communication was aggressive, their reasoning inconsistent, and only persistence forced them to back down.

While the refund was eventually offered, tenants should be aware: always insist on written evidence, challenge unlawful deductions, and know your rights under the Tenant Fees Act.

Close to Paddington tube station, Hyde Park and Kensington Gardens if any are where you need to be. Notting Hill and Holland Park also not too far.

Tea and coffee provided in room but not 5 star quality. Chipped glasses too.

Bathroom small but well fitted and functional with powerful shower and sink tap. No robes or slippers, expected there to be for a 5 star hotel but that didn't affect us for 1 night.

Discovered when in the shower the shampoo was empty, not the end of the world but a 5 star hotel should pay more attention to detail.

one_star_reviews.text:
DO NOT USE FOR BED BUGS!!!

This is honestly one of the worst companies I’ve dealt with for pest control and despite what they say their workers are not properly qualified. You have to be part of the BPCA and sit extensive exams to be able to have access to buy certain pesticides and equipment. This company may be able to skate by on basic jobs. But for proper pest control they are useless.

I paid £560 for heat treatment and when the guy arrived he identified a wall panel board as the source. I asked should It not be removed?. He said it did not need to be removed today it can be removed tomorrow. He then conducted the heat treatment, after it was finished he said “that’s it they are all dead they cannot survive the heat” which is very unprofessional because any professional knows bed bugs are not that easy. As I was talking with him and he said that I saw several crawl up the wall on the bed panels.

Also when conducting heat treatment he did not go to the panel and check the actual temperature of the panel to make sure it reached lethal levels he just checked the overall room temperature.

I asked if he can help me remove these panels after the heat treatment based on the fact 2 ran up the wall right after he finished. Once removed we saw there were several alive hiding behind the panel from the heat.

I ended up going with pest UK which was more expensive but now I understand why. When James (pest Uk) came I explained to him the situation and he asked straight away “did they dismantle the bed”. It was only at this point that I realised he had not, nor did he say the bed was the source.

James (pest uk) dismantled the bed and found several in the bed frame. The heat treatment did not penetrate because the bed should have been dismantled. Below you can see a picture of the heat treatment with the panel in place and the bed still in place.

When I spoke to fantastic services asking for some kind of refund they said dismantling furniture is outside the scope of their responsibility and that I had a “heavy infestation” so I should book and pay for more visits. ( this lack lustre treatment approach feels intentional to make you pay more, as any professional would know the heat treatment was compromised from the start due to bed not being properly inspected and wall panels left as hiding spot).

However James at Pest UK said it was not a heavy infestation and showed me pictures of true heavy infestations and made it known that the heat treatment failed because he did not dismantle the bed so they can hide in cold spots, as well as hiding in the panel he instructed to leave in place!

Avoid this company because whatever price they tell you, you’ll end up paying double for bed bugs because they are not thorough! & when you raise an issue they will just blame it on you.

In the attached photos you can see how fantastic services treated the room with all hot spots in place and also instructed me not to remove known wall panel harbourage until the next day. The pictures of the bed dismantled are from Pest Uk and you can see how many were missed and the bed was a harbourage that was missed by Fantastic services, as well as the picture of the room being treated by Pest UK with no bed frame vs room with everything in it (fantastic services). I was told that the fantastic services technician will inform me what to throw away, he did say to throw away the wall panel but to do it the next day “after treatment” and he said absolutely nothing about the bed.

Take my experience as a warning.

Hermione Williams of New Square Chambers was instructed through my solicitor to represent me at an FDR hearing in November 2023.

In my experience, the service fell below the standard I reasonably expected during an already stressful and unfamiliar court process.

The position statement prepared for the hearing contained multiple errors, including an address, a date of death, and a (Will) date repeated throughout the document unrelated to my case, that had been filed at court prior to the errors being corrected.

These mistakes were only corrected after I brought them to counsel’s attention, which affected my confidence in the preparation and level of care in preparing my case. The court consent order also contained errors.

During the hearing, I found aspects of communication to be inappropriate and unprofessional. I raised a formal complaint through chambers, who accepted that comments made during the hearing were inappropriate and that counsel should apologise. As there were multiple other issues under my complaint and I remained dissatisfied with chambers’ response, I referred the matter to the Legal Ombudsman in May 2024.

In the Ombudsman’s final decision dated 15 April 2026, two complaints were upheld, relating to document errors and unprofessional comments. A small financial remedy was awarded in relation to the document errors.

While not all aspects of my complaint were upheld, I accepted the Ombudsman’s decision in order to bring the matter to a close.

Absolutely shocking service from start to finish. I would strongly advise anyone considering using this company to look elsewhere.

We booked and paid £750 for transport for 25 people to Cheshire and back. The day before the trip, we were told that our original 25-seater bus had been taken into the workshop due to mechanical issues. We were then moved onto replacement vehicles, which was frustrating but something we were willing to work with.

However, just 20 minutes before departure on the day of the trip, we received another call informing us that one of the replacement buses had been involved in a crash and that only 16 passengers could travel. This left nine people scrambling to find alternative transport at the last minute.

The problems didn’t end there. When it came to getting home, we were effectively left stranded in Cheshire. Nobody was brought home by the company, and our group was left waiting around for hours with poor phone signal and no proper solution offered. We had no choice but to arrange our own transport home.

As a result of the company’s failure to provide the service we had paid for, we ended up spending around £400 extra on taxis and alternative transport. This was on top of the £750 we had already paid for the booking.

To add insult to injury, the company has only offered a £500 refund. Considering they failed to provide the full service, left us stranded, and caused hundreds of pounds of additional expenses, this offer is completely unacceptable.

This was genuinely a horror trip caused entirely by poor planning, unreliable vehicles, last-minute cancellations, and a complete lack of contingency plans. The stress, inconvenience, and extra cost placed on our group were unbelievable.

I would not recommend this company to anyone. The service was unreliable, unprofessional, and one of the worst experiences I have ever had with a transport provider.

Complaint

Absolutely avoid this dealership if you value basic customer service or professionalism.

I was told to attend my appointment between 8:00–8:30am so my car could be seen ASAP because I’d only had the vehicle for 2 and a half weeks and was already experiencing issues. The appointment was booked as an all-day appointment (as that was the only option available) and I was also specifically told the booking had been marked as a PRIORITY appointment. Despite this, when I arrived at Vauxhall Chingford, nobody approached me or helped with the check-in process for 4 and a half hours.

After waiting for hours with no updates, it became clear the car hadn’t even gone into the workshop because nobody had taken the keys. One employee openly questioned another colleague, Nick, asking why the keys hadn’t been collected yet and stated: “Without taking the keys out first we can’t do anything.” He then added that Nick had worked there for 2 months and “should know this.” Even after this was raised internally, Nick never apologised once for the poor customer service or the delay.

What made the experience even worse was the attitude from staff throughout the day. I was repeatedly spoken down to and treated as though I knew nothing about cars whenever I questioned what was happening with my vehicle. Instead of showing understanding or professionalism, I was made to feel dismissed and patronised for simply asking for updates on a car I had only owned for 2 and a half weeks.

What makes this even more frustrating is that Nick had apparently read the note left on the system the day before confirming this booking was supposed to be treated as a priority — yet it clearly was not.

After finally chasing things up myself and through the dealership that sold me the car, the vehicle suddenly went into the workshop and diagnostics were completed within around 20 minutes, proving it could have been dealt with much sooner. Instead, I spent around 6 hours total at the dealership for something that should have been prioritised from the beginning.

The communication throughout was poor, staff were abrupt and dismissive, and nobody seemed willing to take accountability for the situation. Considering I was sent to the Chingford branch because the Chesterfield branch is a 3-hour drive away, the lack of care and understanding made the experience even more frustrating.

Overall, one of the worst dealership experiences I’ve had. Completely unacceptable treatment, especially for a customer who had only just purchased the vehicle.

A very poor experience - I'd urge caution.
I was offered a price so far below market value that it was genuinely shocking. When I pushed back, the justifications given simply didn't stack up - a quick search afterwards confirmed the offer was a fraction of what the item was actually worth.
Before you go anywhere near this place, look up your item on eBay. CEX, literally on the same street, offered significantly more - in some cases 2–3x the cash price, and even higher for store credit. There is no good reason to use this shop if getting a fair price matters to you.
What concerns me most is that this kind of pricing targets people who are under financial pressure and may not know better. That's not sharp business - it's exploitative. Do your research, compare your options, and don't let yourself be taken advantage of.
And if you're buying rather than selling, be warned: items I've seen sold here have had undisclosed faults, and when it comes to getting support, repairs, or refunds, the attitude is unhelpful at best. You're on your own the moment money changes hands.

SCAM — Misrepresented Hotel Name Used to Trap Guests into Non-Refundable Cancellation

I booked what was listed online as "The Marble Arch Hotel" and paid £1,000 for 4 nights. Upon arrival, I discovered the actual property is Park Grand Mayfair — a completely different name to what was advertised.
I immediately raised this at check-in and requested a refund, as I had not booked Park Grand Mayfair. The staff told me I needed to cancel the booking first in order to process a refund. I cancelled on the spot, trusting their instruction.
What followed was 45 days of chasing with no meaningful response — only to be told at the end that no refund is permitted because I had cancelled. They used their own refund instruction as the mechanism to forfeit my entire payment.

This is a straightforward trap:

1- Advertise under a different name
2- Tell the guest to cancel to get a refund
3- Deny the refund because the guest cancelled

I lost £1,000 and received zero nights' accommodation.
Booking reference: 260578659
I have since raised this with my card provider and am pursuing it through the appropriate consumer channels. I would strongly advise anyone to verify the exact legal trading name of any hotel before booking, and to never cancel on the hotel's verbal instruction without written confirmation of the refund first.
Zero stars. Avoid entirely.

As a private seller, I relied on Noonans’ established reputation to manage and protect my high-value asset. Unfortunately, the strategic guidance provided by their specialist team resulted in a severe financial shortfall that directly forced the cancellation of my planned summer holiday. I consigned a rare 1942 Iraqi 10 Dinars banknote, which Noonans initially appraised with an official estimate of £2,600–£3,200. Following my rejection of a provisional post-sale offer of £2,400, their department explicitly proposed in writing to reoffer the lot at a “slightly lower estimate,” reassuring me that their new live bidding interface would successfully “entice early bids.” Furthermore, I was verbally assured that a low ball figure would not be accepted. I even want as far as getting the note PMG graded at my own expense. While I understand the systemic risks inherent to a no-reserve auction, I only went forward because I relied upon these explicit professional assurances. As a non-expert client, I trusted their specialists to defend the baseline value of my property. I did not anticipate that following their exact directive would yield an unacceptable hammer price of £1700 and a net payout of just £1,488.20. Instead of a modest reduction, Noonans reduced the low estimate by 23%. Down from £2600 to £2,000. Their live bidding system failed entirely to protect the asset. The note was sold at a price nearly £1,000 below the initial valuation floor established by the house. Private consignors should exercise extreme caution: relying on the professional advice of Noonans’ specialists can result in a significant financial deficit and substantial personal distress. In my view, the house failed to uphold a reasonable standard of professional care.

The whole situation just makes me sad. My summer is completely ruined. If they were going to slash the valuation floor from £2,600 to £2,000 a month before the auction, then wouldn’t it have been worth giving me a call?

The automated email I received wasn’t acceptable given the significance of the matter—this was a high-value consignment and I needed a clear, specific explanation, not a generic automated message. I know some of the blame rests with me. If only I had seen the email in time. I would’ve immediately pulled the banknote from the auction. The whole situation just upsets me. Trusting you was a massive mistake and it’s cost me nearly £1000.

EDIT. Noonans’ response is a blatant attempt to rewrite history. At no point did their specialist actually advise me that the £2,400 after-sale offer was a “good offer.” Furthermore, they did not manually consult me about the major price drop—they simply informed me about a 23% reduction in a cold, automated email notification.

Consider their logic: If noonans treats a 23% drop as “slight.” That means if you consign a high-value asset worth £100,000 and market conditions change—resulting in a reduction of £23,000—they can protect themselves by sending an automated email rather than providing direct, meaningful communication. If you’re an older person, or anyone who doesn’t spend the day monitoring their inbox (or who is dealing with an emergency), don’t assume they will proactively protect your property or pick up the phone.

I took a major financial loss by relying on their human expertise. My advice to anyone dealing with this house is clear: if your item is worth £100 or more, never proceed without a formal reserve price in place. Don’t rely on their initial estimates, don’t rely on their automated communication, and don’t trust them in general.

Where, exactly, in our email thread were these risks explained? Your team actively persuaded me that re-entering the auction was a good course of action. They specifically described the offer as being at the lower end of the estimate—they did not say it was a good offer. Now, instead of conducting a genuine and fair investigation into my case, management appears to have skimmed over my complaint. They are choosing to ignore their staff’s errors and deny responsibility.

$6300 CDN worth of items were paid for the same day I was invoiced. Despite me requesting immediate shipment they needed reminding of this a week later, then shipping was immediate. This is not my problem.

The shipping terms stated FedEx would be the carrier which would have been great as I have never had problems with them and they are always fast. To my surprise DHL tracking info was sent to me. It actually wasn’t sent from Noonans, DHL contacted me and I didn’t know what it was for at first.

There has recently been over 2 weeks of “Shipment on hold” notices because the items were not sent with the proper declarations or invoices or both, or anything? After one week of these notices DHL requested the duty (plus fees) which I paid in full, but things still didn’t start moving. I sent Canada Customs and DHL every single document that I had but it was not enough to clear the items because the invoices I have do not state what the items are, only lot numbers, etc… “Shipment on hold” updates continue most days. Some days DHL takes a break from sending them.

33 days after paying my invoice in full I still do not know if this will ever arrive or is being sent back after I paid the duty.  I can say for certain that this has been the worst shipping experience I have ever had from anyone, by far.  Noonans has not responded to a single email since the shipment was sent.

Best case scenario, after a couple months of phone calls and emails to DHL, Canada Customs and Noonans I get the items and simply paid way too much for shipping, fees and insurance, which was about $200 Canadian.  I probably spent 4+ hours on hold with DHL only to be disconnected every single time I got through. Their call back feature is also not working right now. Funny how this was the most I have ever paid for shipping in my life and the level of service has been the lowest, by far.

Noonans appears very professional, but looks can be deceiving. If you can find your items elsewhere, you will probably have a much smoother experience overall and you may actually even get the items you paid for in a timely manner!  There has been other times where Noonans either left out some of my items from a shipment or charged me VAT on top of the Canadian Customs duty I had to pay.  I wish people would consign their items to other Auction houses.

Sorry if this all sounds harsh, but I’m simply asking for the items that I paid for.

Not recommended.

In April, I successfully bid at an auction and was able to purchase a coin.

After examining it in person for the first time, I began to have doubts about its authenticity and contacted Noonans to ask whether they had verified the coin’s authenticity or if they could at least tell me something about its provenance. Three weeks have now passed, and despite a follow-up request, I have not yet received a response from Noonans.

I will now send the purchased coin to NGC or have its authenticity verified by other experts. If its authenticity cannot be confirmed, I will demand a refund.

After my experience with DCK Solicitors, I believe people should know exactly what they might face before signing contracts or paying large legal fees.

I paid around £2,500 to DCK Solicitors to assist with my immigration matter, trusting them with a case that directly affected my future and my family’s life in the UK.

Unfortunately, my application was later rejected as invalid. Throughout the process, there was confusion regarding key issues relating to documents and the handling of the application. Following later discussions with the firm, concerns surrounding mistakes in the application process were acknowledged. As a client, I expected important issues to be identified and addressed clearly from the outset. Instead, I found myself trying to understand major aspects of my own case after the fact.

What concerned me most was what happened next. After already paying approximately £2,500, I contacted the firm to discuss the situation and next steps. I was then informed that a further payment of approximately £1,000 would be needed to continue and effectively redo work on the case. After investing significant money, trust and time, this left me feeling frustrated and questioning the level of care and responsibility taken with my matter.

Eventually I lost confidence in allowing the firm to continue handling my case and decided to proceed independently.

My advice to anyone considering DCK Solicitors: ask detailed questions, understand possible additional costs, and ensure everything is clearly confirmed in writing before signing anything. Immigration matters affect families and futures, and clients deserve clarity and confidence throughout the process.

This review reflects my personal experience.

I got married two months ago, and as someone who usually wears braids, I wanted a different look for my wedding day. I booked a consultation online. Although the salon atmosphere and the reception were not very welcoming, the stylist I met was friendly and engaging.
I explained exactly what I wanted and emphasised that I was very nervous about wearing a lace wig for the first time. My biggest concern was the lace showing or the hairline looking unnatural in photos. I was reassured that this would not happen due to the quality of the wig and the stylist’s expertise, so I went ahead with the purchase.

At my fitting appointment, scheduled for 1 pm, the stylist arrived late and did not begin until around 1:30 pm. My wig was handed to me in a plastic bag to hold while I waited. I had booked a cornrow and sew-in install. During the appointment, the stylist barely spoke to me and made very little effort to help me feel comfortable as a first-time client. The atmosphere felt awkward and impersonal for most of the appointment.
The install itself seemed fine initially, although I specifically asked for the perimeter of the wig to be sewn down. The stylist advised that this was unnecessary because the wig was glueless and should hold fine on its own. Since I only planned to wear the wig briefly at the time, I accepted the advice. The stylist was not rude, but she did come across as abrupt and not particularly friendly.

Three weeks later, I returned for my wedding-day reinstall and booked the glued-down service. Again, I booked an early appointment, and again the stylist arrived late and was not very welcoming. The install took over three hours; by the end, it did not look right. The wig appeared lopsided and the middle parting was uneven. After sitting there for so long and not being able to properly assess it until I got home, I decided to leave it as it was.
The following morning — on my wedding day — I woke up to find the front of the wig crusty, with the glue already lifting. This was exactly the situation I had expressed concern about during my consultation. I tried my best to fix it myself by cleaning it up and using a hairdryer to dry the glue further.

Unfortunately, I have now received my wedding photos, and I am genuinely devastated. The lace is clearly visible and looks crusty in many of the pictures. After only two wears, the wig is also shedding excessively, becoming frizzy, and tangling badly. I have not worn it since my wedding day.
Overall, I am deeply disappointed, especially considering this was for such an important occasion. I had trusted the salon’s expertise and reassurance, but the final result did not meet the expectations that were set.

I received the wig in poor condition and contacted the company immediately with photos requesting a return label and refund. Despite multiple follow-ups, I have received no response from customer service. I am currently giving the company an opportunity to resolve the issue directly, which is why I have not posted the photos publicly at this stage.

I really never thought I would end up having to ask publicly for help like this but I have no idea what I can do at this point.
The problem with abuse is that everyone shys away or enables the abuser.

My children were meant to be returned home to me three days ago, and they still haven’t come home. I miss them desperately and feel completely worn down by what has become a repeated pattern of abuse during school holidays over the past three years.

I know many parents suffer painful consequences after the breakdown of a relationship, and I never wanted my own situation to become something spoken about publicly. But right now I feel exhausted and out of options trying to resolve this peacefully.

There are court orders in place, including orders allowing police involvement, but because my children are still very young, I am trying everything I can to avoid this becoming even more distressing and traumatic for them.
I have reached out to Strand Contemporary Art Gallery in Hastings because someone connected to the situation is currently away with my former partner while my children have not been returned home. I also don’t know how much they fully understand about the seriousness of what is happening. For context, my boys are 3, 5 & 7 so Im unwilling for their father to be arrested infront of them especially given everything they have already witnessed.

I am not trying to create hostility or shame anybody publicly. I am simply asking, compassionately and humanely, for help facilitating a safe, calm handover so my children can come home to their mum without further escalation.

I know this is uncomfortable for everybody connected to it. I just want this cycle to stop and for the children to be returned peacefully and safely.

I applied for a Funding Circle FlexiPay card to finance the purchase of some equipment. Throughout the application and sales process, I received multiple follow-up communications, which gave me confidence to proceed with the purchase. Based on my understanding, I planned to pay a deposit from my own funds and spread the remaining balance over 12 months using the FlexiPay facility.

However, when I came to complete the transaction, I discovered that the advertised transaction charges only applied to a three-month repayment term, not the 12-month term I intended to use. As a result, the purchase fee increased dramatically from around 6% to approximately 22%.

I feel this was not made sufficiently clear during the sales process and that the product was misrepresented, whether intentionally or otherwise. Had I understood the true cost of financing over my preferred term, I would have reconsidered my purchasing decision.

I have lodged a formal complaint and understand that it may take up to eight weeks to receive a response. In the meantime, I would urge anyone considering this product to read the terms and conditions very carefully and ensure they fully understand how the fees vary depending on the repayment period.

I am hugely disappointed with this experience and now find myself committed to a purchase that I cannot reverse.

one_star_reviews.text:
We had booked two tables through First Table: one for three people and one for two people (four adults and a 4-year-old child in total). Unfortunately, the person in charge at the door was extremely unprofessional.

From the moment we arrived, he seemed determined not to seat us together. We tried to be as flexible as possible and suggested several solutions: squeezing into a table for four, adding an extra chair, sitting outside, waiting until a larger table became available, or even giving up the First Table discount altogether, which appeared to be his main concern. None of these options were accepted.

I have never experienced anything like this before. I work in the hospitality industry myself, and customer service is built on finding solutions and making guests feel welcome and valued. In this case, there was absolutely no effort to accommodate us. We remained calm, polite, and reasonable throughout the entire interaction. We did not argue, complain, or make a scene; we simply tried to understand and find a workable solution together.

Overall, it felt as though every possible effort was made to prevent us from sitting together rather than helping us enjoy our meal.

Thankfully, the evening was saved when we went across the street to Bricco e Bacco instead. The food was delicious, especially the pasta dishes and meat, the staff were wonderful, and the atmosphere was lovely.

As for Norma, I honestly wouldn’t recommend it even to my worst enemy based on the way we were treated upon arrival.

P.S. You can keep the £16 reservation fee and spend it on an ice cream for the staff. 😂

Disappointing Customer Service and Unwelcoming Experience

We made a reservation on First Table and arrived looking forward to enjoying a family meal. Our group consisted of 5 people: 4 adults and 1 small child. From the beginning of the interaction, however, the staff member who assisted us was dismissive and unnecessarily rude.

We had made two reservations and were informed that the only available table was supposedly for 3 people, despite it clearly appearing large enough to accommodate 4. Since we were dining with a small child, we suggested that adding an extra chair could be a simple solution. The staff member immediately rejected the idea and repeatedly stated that it was impossible, without making any effort to help or explore alternatives.

Trying to be flexible, we even offered to cancel the First Table booking and pay full price if that would allow us to be seated at a table for 5. Once again, we were told it was impossible because the restaurant was full. What was most disappointing was that no alternatives were offered. We were not given the option to wait, nor was there any attempt to find a solution or accommodate our group in any way.

Throughout the entire interaction, we remained polite, respectful, and cooperative. At no point were we demanding, argumentative, or disrespectful. We simply tried to understand the situation and proposed reasonable alternatives. Unfortunately, those efforts were met with a negative attitude and an unwillingness to help.

We fully understand that restaurants have policies and capacity limits, and we respect that. However, good customer service is about communication, professionalism, and treating guests with courtesy. Instead, we were made to feel unwelcome from the moment we arrived.

The experience left us wondering whether First Table customers are treated differently. If that is the case, perhaps the restaurant should reconsider participating in the program. Every customer, regardless of how they book, deserves to be treated with the same level of respect and hospitality.

After being repeatedly refused any reasonable solution and feeling completely unwelcome, we decided to leave and dine elsewhere. It was a very disappointing experience and unfortunately not one we would recommend.

DO NOT HOST A CHILDREN’S PARTY HERE – PARENTS ARE BEING CAUGHT OUT BY THE PARKING SYSTEM.

I’ve been visiting Bewl Water for years, mainly because of the soft play facilities for young children, but the parking situation has become completely unreasonable.

Recently, I attended a child’s birthday party and attempted to pay the very expensive parking fee for only 1.5 hours. Unfortunately, their parking app would not work. I went into reception to ask if I could simply pay at the desk, but was told this was not possible. As a result, I later received a £60 parking charge notice despite making genuine efforts to pay.

I appealed the ticket and provided screenshots showing the app failure, but the appeal was rejected. I also contacted Bewl Water directly with feedback and have followed up twice since, yet I have still received no response at all.

What makes this even more concerning is the lack of reasonable alternatives for customers. Not everyone owns a smartphone, has mobile signal, bank app access, or is comfortable using digital-only payment systems. This could particularly disadvantage elderly visitors, disabled people, or those with accessibility needs. Refusing to accept cash or alternative payment methods while issuing large penalties raises serious questions around fairness, customer service, and inclusivity.

It is incredibly disappointing to see a family venue operate in a way that feels more focused on parking revenue than supporting paying visitors. Sadly, after years of visiting, I will no longer attend events or accept invitations to Bewl Water in future.

one_star_reviews.text:
Let me save you the trouble of making a reservation here — the restaurant might do that for you anyway.

Two months out, we booked a table for four at Sette. Twenty-four hours before our Wednesday reservation, we received an email informing us it had been canceled. No explanation. A phone call to the restaurant yielded the truth: a private event had taken priority, and they were “sorry for the mixup.” Against our better judgment, we rebooked for Thursday.

We should have trusted our instincts.

We arrived at 7:30pm for our reservation. By 9pm, as we were finishing our meal, the room looked exactly as it did when we walked in — two occupied tables out of 20+. Not a single additional party had been seated in nearly two hours. The photo attached to this review was taken at 9pm and speaks for itself. This is a flagship restaurant inside one of London’s most expensive hotels, steps from Hyde Park, on a Thursday evening. The emptiness wasn’t intimate — it was telling. The room is genuinely beautiful, which somehow makes it worse. You could film a post-apocalyptic movie here and not change a thing.

The crudo tasting arrived with fish that was competently sourced but cut so imprecisely it was impossible to eat with the spoon it was served on. A minor grievance in isolation. Foreshadowing in retrospect.

The lobster pasta contained what I can only describe as 2.5 marble-sized pieces of lobster swimming in a sauce with all the depth of a puddle. For the price, you’d expect the lobster to at least be detectable. The amatriciana, to its credit, was genuinely good — a reminder that someone in that kitchen knows what they’re doing, which somehow makes everything else more baffling.

Then there was the ribeye. A pastrami-cured ribeye at £55, ordered medium. The photo attached to this review requires no caption — grey throughout, edge to edge, with the texture of something you’d find at a cobbler rather than a restaurant. No gradient. No pink. Just a uniform monument to indifference, plated and served with apparent confidence. At a neighborhood bistro this would be disappointing. At Bvlgari, it’s inexcusable.

Our server was pleasant and attentive. She was also covering two tables on a Thursday night, so the bar was doing a lot of the work.

The bill came to over £300 for a table of four. That figure, against the backdrop of what was actually delivered — the botched crudo, the ghost lobster, the leather ribeye, the post-apocalyptic dining room — is the most surreal part of the evening.

Sette means “seven” in Italian. After this meal, we’d suggest a rebrand to Uno — a more honest reflection of the star rating this restaurant has earned.

Review for Barrister Philip Bowen
Title: Serious Concerns About Quality of Representation in Financial Remedy Case.
I am writing this review to share my experience with barrister Philip Bowen, who represented me at my final divorce financial remedy hearing. Although his biography and professional profile appear impressive, the representation I received fell far short of what I expected at such a critical stage of my case.
From the outset, I felt I was not properly prepared or advised for the final hearing. Several central issues were not clearly identified, raised, or challenged, including:
• the distinction between pension assets and capital assets,
• the proper treatment of my non-matrimonial savings, and
• the inconsistencies in the respondent’s financial disclosure.
Another major concern was that Mr Bowen decided not to pursue the issue of the gold and jewellery held by my ex-wife without consulting me.
When the judge, due to time constraints, requested written submissions from both parties, I was extremely disappointed by the quality of Mr Bowen’s work. His written submissions were, in my view, weak, superficial, and failed to set out the key arguments of my case. At the handing down of judgment, the judge even remarked that the submission was “very brave”, which spoke volumes. In stark contrast, the submissions prepared by the other side’s barrister were clear, detailed, and far more persuasive. The disparity between the two was obvious.
The result was a financial outcome that has had a serious negative effect on my housing and retirement position. I left the process feeling that essential arguments were never properly put before the court and that opportunities to correct clear errors were missed.
This has been one of the most distressing legal experiences of my life. I believe it is only fair to share my experience so others can make an informed choice when selecting representation for financial remedy proceedings.

one_star_reviews.text:
Very disappointing experience.
Booked myself and my daughter in for a ‘luxury spa experience and massage’ there was no luxury in this. Advertised as a spa, is just a small gym with some facilities which everyone has access too.

Massive floor to ceiling windows from the gym overlooking the pool so the people on the treadmill are watching you ‘relax’. A dirty looking jacuzzi and a small cold pool where people are doing their work out lanes so you can not relax or be comfortable.

No relaxation area, the area with chairs in the pictures is outside. So you have to come out of the ‘spa’ area, changing area, round the gym equipment and sit outside with people walking back and forth around you in your bikini?? No thank you.
This is very misrepresented as other reviews have stated. Not a spa experience I’m used it at all.
Not somewhere I would ever come back to or recommend.
Mainly because of the manager who was extremely rude, aggressive and downright nasty. I explained this was for myself and my daughters birthday, she is 17 and never had a spa day before and also she is extremely uncomfortable with confrontation, this did not stop the manager being rude and unwilling to understand my points made about this basically being false advertising, if they advertised as a gym, then fair, they advertise as a spa, with an optional gym. Not the same.
Was told they would check CCTV to see if we used anything, told it’s not a £400 experience and I should basically be grateful for this at £200. Ridiculous. Never even made it to the massages because I was way too uncomfortable to allow this woman to touch me by then, which she confirmed she felt the same.

Don’t waste your time or money. So annoyed we did.

Awful. Its not a spa its a gym with a few spa like facilities. The pool is advertised as part of the so called spa but is being used mainly by gym members to do laps so you feel like you cannot lay in the pool and relax because you have to move out the way. People are waiting to use the hot tub so again u feel rushed. The relaxation room is just a few chairs outside so you have to walk past the gym goers and sit outside in your bikini or robe. There are huge windows the size of the wall where everyone from the gym can just look in on you in the pool and Jacuzzi area, It feels invasive. It should be advertised as a gym that has access to some spa perks. But it is not a spa. One of the massage workers was very rude. She had attitude, couldn’t take the criticism even though we were incredibly patient with the convo and were simply sharing why we didn’t enjoy our time. As someone who hates confrontation I felt incredibly awkward and almost like I wanted to cry. There was no welcoming. We were told we would get free drinks due to it being our birthdays and there were no workers around to even offer it. Unwelcoming. We were the only people there for the spa purpose and felt out of place. Id never go again and id recommend you go somewhere else. I wish id had read the bad reviews before going. ruined my birthday.

They ruined my hair.

I had a perm with Svetlana, and the result was a complete disaster, as shown in the photos. My hair is now half straight, half wavy, and visibly damaged from the perm process. Parts of it look burnt and completely failed to take the curl.

Instead of taking responsibility, they immediately started looking for excuses. First, they blamed my highlights, which makes no sense because even the back sections of my hair that didn't have highlights are not curly at all. Then they claimed the issue was that I had dyed my hair the day before the appointment. The problem with that excuse is that I specifically called the salon beforehand to ask what I should avoid doing before a perm, and nobody mentioned that colouring my hair beforehand would be an issue. On top of that, I told Svetlana during the appointment that I had dyed my hair the day before. If that was genuinely a concern, she should have refused the service and told me to come back in a couple of weeks instead of proceeding and damaging my hair.

Another issue is that I specifically asked for curls. What I got was small waves on half of my head is the exact result I said I did not want.

To make matters worse, they also burned the skin on my neck during the process.

What shocked me most was their attitude afterwards. Not only did they refuse to accept responsibility, they initially refused to give me a refund. It took a huge argument before they agreed, and even then they tried to give me only a partial refund. I had to argue again just to get my money back in full.

Despite damaging my hair, they didn't offer any treatment, bond repair, conditioning treatment, or even a moisturising mask. Most importantly, nobody apologised.

The poor quality of the service is one thing, but the complete lack of professionalism, accountability, and customer care made the experience even worse.

This was a family occasion, during which we ordered plenty of food and drinks, spending a considerable amount in the process.

Our group of four was seated directly next to another group of four and their two dogs, which meant we were unnecessarily in such close proximity when there were tables free adjacent to us.

Secondly, and not unrelated, is the number of dogs in the restaurant in general. While I would question the appropriateness of having dogs in a pub in the first place, I understand there are some who feel this is permissible. However, I certainly do not feel this is appropriate in a restaurant setting. As a result of being placed directly next to the group of four with two dogs, one of these dogs was in my space under the table for virtually the entire meal, despite several half-hearted attempts by the owner to bring it closer to her.

Furthermore, on one visit to the table, our server was stroking the dog before bringing our food out. I don’t really want a server stroking/handling/playing with a dog before bringing food to our table.

The service in general was lacking in various aspects. Our server did not have a grasp of the food and drinks menu nor an understanding of when to clear tables and instead left multiple items on the table across courses.

In terms of the menu itself, I was quite disappointed to find that the roast ham had sold out by 15:00 on a Sunday. I would have expected that the roasts are central to a menu on this day in particular and stocked accordingly.

Nevertheless, I ordered the roast chicken - and I have to say it was pretty mediocre. To me it seemed greasy, maybe even undercooked. Not to the point of being unsafe though I might add. Far too many bones and the choice of vegetables did not complement the dish very well at all. They were hard and relatively small in portion size. Meanwhile I counted less than 10 chips on my mum’s fish and chips.

In terms of the layout, I think it’s a disaster having two shuffleboards directly overlooking the tables and the noise from these is not conducive to the sort of atmosphere that I’m looking for when dining in a restaurant setting.

In sum, I was incredibly underwhelmed by the experience overall. This was only worsened by what I felt was an exorbitant bill at the end, which was not a reflection of the quality of food, drinks, service or attention to detail - £5.10 for a Pepsi, for example, is just plain gouging in my opinion. I couldn’t help but feeling ripped off. Short changed.

My disappointment was compounded by the fact that I wrote to the business with constructive feedback and my email was ignored.

There are an abundance of dining options in the area and it is details like those I’ve outlined above which truly separate the best from the rest.
